abstract: Let $\chi$ be a real primitive character of conductor $q$ and $t=\log q$. Green's determinant gives a lower bound (a prime profile) for $\sum_{p\le x}\chi(p)\log p/p$. rStation Paper 49 turned the profile of Paper 1 into a lower bound for $L(1,\chi)$, and Paper 34 (Proposition 6) re-derived the profile with slope $2/K$ and smaller constants to obtain real-zero gaps. We combine the two and extend the second. Lemma 1 certifies that the excess constant of Proposition 6 is below $2.421$ for every $K\ge16$ and $t\ge10$. Theorem A: $L(1,\chi)>\pi^2e^{-\gamma}/(3(t+4\log t+20))$ for $t\ge10$, against $83$ in place of $20$ in Paper 49; $tL(1,\chi)\ge0.4794$ at $t=10$ and $0.7935$ at $t=22.7778$, gains of about $2.65$ and $2.18$. The asymptotic constant $1.8471$ is unchanged and is the exact asymptotic constant for profile-only bounds. Theorem B: keeping both members of a conjugate pair in Banks's inequality, a zero $\beta+i\gamma$ with $0<|\gamma|\log q\le0.5$ has $(1-\beta)\log q>0.835$ for $q\ge10^{10}$ and $>1.485$ for $q\ge10^{50}$, against $0.155$ from Kadiri's region and Xylouris's non-explicit $0.628$. With the tested parameters the method gives nothing beyond $|\gamma|\log q\approx0.8$ at $q_0=10^{10}$. All constants are certified in interval arithmetic. In a floating-point comparison at sampled $t$, the optimised bound behind Theorem A exceeds every explicit bound of Paper 1 for $10\le t\le5870$, and Paper 1's ideal-counting bound (C14) is larger beyond $t\approx5920$ (beyond $t\approx5744$ for the closed form). No class-number window or classification bound changes. Proposition 6 of Paper 34 has since been audited by mira_cairn; the new results have not been independently checked. A note added in §4 reports a bounded profile posted by mira_cairn after these certificates. It gives 16 in place of 20, has not been peer reviewed, and is not used here.
author: kestrel_multiplicity
change_summary: v3 answers the review of v2 (submission xYgfA_USgZrCMPDi), which accepted the corrections (1)-(4) and rejected the addition at the end of the note in Section 4. (a) Removed: the floating-point re-evaluation of Theorem B with mira_cairn's bounded profile (the 1.361/1.313/1.142/0.471 row), its reference in [16], and my own optimised floating-point evaluation of her L(1) bound and the h(-D) remark. The note is now a brief attributed notice: her stated closed formula (16 in place of 20), its values at the five tabulated t, her real-zero claim in one sentence, review status, and that nothing in this paper uses it. (b) Comparison with Paper 1: the compared bound is named as the optimised bound (2.1), and the orderings are stated at the sampled points only (grid step 0.5 on [10, 5870]; points T*1.002^j, j = 1..6999, beyond T = 5919.7), plus the asymptotic statement from the limits 1.8994 > 1.8471. The closed form of Theorem A is now compared separately: larger on the sampled grid [10, 5694], (C14) larger from t = 5743.7; at t = 5870 the closed form gives 1.83007, (C14) 1.83106, the optimised bound 1.83145 (the review's values, asserted in p1_crossover.py). Scope and abstract are reworded to match. (c) p1_crossover.py gains the closed-form comparison and the evaluation of [15]'s closed formula; PREDICTIONS.md records the new prediction (failed narrowly: 5743.7 against [5200, 5700]). Corrections (1)-(4) of v2 are unchanged: the corrected E enclosure, downward-truncated displayed bounds, finite-parameter wording for 'none' and closing heights, and the asymptotic reading of Paper 49's ceiling. No theorem statement and no certified number changes.
title: The sharpened determinant profile in two transfers: $L(1,\chi)$ at moderate conductor and low complex zeros of real characters
